question: Purpose of currentThread() in multithreading, with a small program.
title: Who Am I, Thread?
hook: Many nurses, same instructions, one name badge each. currentThread() reads yours.
answer: Thread.currentThread() is a static method of the Thread class.
It returns a reference to the thread that is currently executing that line of code.
Use it to get or set that thread's name and priority; it is most useful when many threads share the same code, to know which one is running.

Program: main prints Thread.currentThread().getName() -> main; class Worker extends Thread { public void run() { System.out.println(Thread.currentThread().getName()); } } started with new Worker().start() prints Thread-0.
Output: main, Thread-0 (same code, different thread, different name).
